One deliberate workflow

From a blank project to a validated player.

Kéire connects installation, authoring, simulation, content cooking, packaging, and diagnosis through boundaries you can inspect and reason about.

01

Hub owns projects and toolchains.

Keep editor versions independent, resolve compatible components, and observe resumable tasks without mixing engine binaries into project content.

02

Author with live context.

Scenes, shaders, materials, animation, audio, input, C#, and VFX stay connected to diagnostics and recoverable state.

03

Ship deterministic content.

Typed identities, stable manifests, explicit package sources, and bounded archives make release output inspectable.

04

Keep last-good state.

Transactional imports, project recovery journals, compilation diagnostics, and safe upgrades are product behavior—not cleanup work postponed until launch.

How work moves

Clear owners at every boundary.

The Hub, Editor, asset pipeline, and runtime collaborate through versioned contracts instead of hidden shared state.

01 / Discover

Choose the right Editor

Hub resolves a verified release and keeps project compatibility visible.

02 / Author

Build with immediate feedback

Focused tools expose validation where the graph, asset, or scene failed.

03 / Validate

Cook exact inputs

Build fingerprints bind assets, scripts, packages, platform, and renderer capability.

04 / Recover

Fail without corruption

Atomic publication and journals preserve the last state known to be valid.

Build in the open

Kéire is substantial, early, and honest about both.
